review_notes: NASA/Commons microgravity boiling video shows vapor bubbles nucleating, growing, coalescing and departing over time. The named concept cannot be inferred from one still frame because the evidence is the growth/departure sequence; no answer-bearing text is visible in the cleaned derivative.

The video contains title cards and visible setup labels naming hydrogel microspring formation, sodium alginate solution, and calcium chloride solution. The visible dynamics are extrusion/microspring formation rather than a clean gelation-front propagation process, so accepting the target would rely too much on source/setup text.

After the opening text, the clip shows a pink fiber/microspring forming and coiling from a capillary. It does not make a propagating gelation or solidification front visually decisive, so the target concept would be source-dependent.

Commons/PLOS microscopy time-lapse shows an early embryo progressing through repeated cleavage divisions into many smaller cells. The visible timestamp is not answer-bearing; the source metadata was stripped. The concept requires observing the temporal division sequence rather than identifying a static embryo.

The NASA Mars video is mostly a science visualization/flyover of planetary surface features, with explanatory arrows and no clear textless segment showing grains moving downslope along a dune slip face. Reject because the dynamic evidence is not sufficient for Dune Slip-Face Avalanche.
